decisive_items: His mother had systemic lupus erythematosus treated with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisolone and was positive for anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La antibodies
antibody testing confirmed high-titer antinuclear antibodies (>1:1000) and 52-kD anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La positivity
His heart rate remained between 60 and 100 bpm
A permanent pacemaker was placed on day 50
response.rationale: Maternal SLE with anti-Ro/La antibodies, infant antibody positivity, bradycardia requiring pacemaker, and progressive pulmonary disease are classic for neonatal lupus. Congenital heart block is a manifestation of neonatal lupus, not the overarching diagnosis. Pneumonia and BPD are secondary or less specific.

rejected.why: Infectious findings were transient and culture-positive episodes resolved; progressive ground-glass opacities with negative cultures and normal inflammatory markers argue against primary pneumonia.
BPD is a chronic lung disease of prematurity, but the CT pattern and clinical course with maternal autoantibodies and cardiac involvement better fit neonatal lupus pulmonary disease.
Congenital heart block is a key feature but is a component of neonatal lupus, not the most likely overall diagnosis.
